payload.title: 20 Greece Wedding Venues From the Islands to Athens
payload.excerpt: This guide groups Greece wedding venues into seven regions, and the right one depends less on the view than on three practical questions: how many guests you are inviting, which kind of ceremony you want, and how those guests will travel.
key_takeaways: Guest count decides the region: Santorini's caldera terraces seat 15 to 60, while venues on the Athens Riviera and in Crete publish space for several hundred.
Exclusive use can mean a chosen event space or the whole hotel, and only a few venues, such as Canaves, Katikies and Melenos, offer the whole hotel.
Curfews, minimum nights and rain plans are rarely published, so have them confirmed in writing before you pay a deposit.
A legal wedding means paperwork, which can include a Certificate of No Impediment, and a summer date means planning around heat, wildfire season and wind-delayed ferries.

faq.q: Which Greek island is best for a wedding with 100 guests?
faq.a: On Santorini, most caldera terraces seat 15 to 60, so 100 guests needs a garden or pool space such as Canaves Epitome's. Mykonos has more room: the Myconian Collection's ballroom seats 270. On Crete, Elounda Beach publishes banquet spaces for several hundred. For 60 to 100 guests with most of them staying on site, look at a Canaves Epitome buyout (53 rooms, up to 170 guests), Angsana Corfu (receptions for 200 and 196 rooms) or One&Only Aesthesis (the Agora Ballroom seats 140).

faq.q: Can you get married at a private villa in Greece?
faq.a: Yes, within a resort. Grace Hotel's 400 sq m villa hosts weddings of up to 15 seated, and Corfu Imperial offers Villa Medusa, with six bedrooms, for intimate celebrations. For the whole property, Canaves and Melenos offer full-hotel bookings.

faq.q: Which Greece wedding venues have rooms for guests on site?
faq.a: All but one on this list. Kokotos Estate lists no guest rooms. Angsana Corfu has 196, and Canaves Epitome's buyout covers 53. Ikos Aria arranges accommodation for up to 30 guests.

faq.q: Is Santorini or Mykonos better for a wedding?
faq.a: Santorini, for the caldera and a smaller guest list. Mykonos, for a bigger party, more beach and more space: the Myconian Collection runs its own guest transfers. Daily ferries link the two.

faq.q: Can Australians have a legal wedding in Greece, or should we marry at home first?
faq.a: Both work. A marriage valid in Greece is usually recognised in Australia, and you may need a Certificate of No Impediment. Some couples marry legally at home and hold a symbolic ceremony in Greece, which several venues here offer.

faq.q: What is the best month for a wedding in Greece?
faq.a: May and October sit outside the June to September wildfire season and the hottest weeks, though some outdoor spaces, such as One&Only Aesthesis's chapel, open only from May to September. In summer, plan an evening ceremony.
